value.name: Rosa breaks the silence
value.description: Rosa finally speaks up after a tense silence, signaling that she has something important to reveal.

value.name: Rosa describes lawyer visit
value.description: Rosa recounts how Mrs. Serrano had her lawyer, Mr. Pinsky, come to the house last September and meet privately with her.
evidence: "Last September," Rosa went on, looking only at Asha. "Mrs. Serrano had her lawyer come to the house. Mr. Pinsky. He came on a Tuesday afternoon and they sat in the back parlor for almost two hours."

value.name: Rosa witnesses paper signing
value.description: Rosa says she was called in at the end of the meeting and signed a paper as a witness alongside Mrs. Adelman.
evidence: "She asked me to come in at the end. She and Mr. Pinsky and a neighbor, Mrs. Adelman from two doors down, and me. Mrs. Serrano signed a paper and we both signed under her name as witnesses. Mrs. Adelman and me."

value.name: Daniel demands paper's purpose
value.description: Daniel presses Rosa to identify what the signed paper was, treating the question as an accusation rather than a request for information.
evidence: "What was the paper," Daniel said. It was not a question.

value.name: Rosa says it changed the will
value.description: Rosa explains that Mrs. Serrano told her the paper was a change to her will.
evidence: "She told me it was a change to her will."

value.name: Daniel presses for details
value.description: Daniel asks whether Mrs. Serrano explained what the will change would do.
evidence: "Did she tell you what it changed."

value.name: Rosa quotes house inheritance condition
value.description: Rosa reports that Mrs. Serrano said she was ensuring the house would go to whoever stayed in it.
evidence: "She said, 'I am making sure the house goes to the person who stays in it.'"

value.name: Asha realizes the implication
value.description: Asha senses the conversation turning toward a significant revelation and notices Lucia's gratitude as evidence.
evidence: "Asha felt the conversation shift its weight, the way a boat shifts when someone unexpected steps aboard. Daniel had gone very still. Lucia had not. Lucia was looking at Rosa with something close to gratitude, and that, Asha noted, was its own piece of evidence."

value.name: Asha notes missing file evidence
value.description: Asha observes that Rosa's account is not included in the case file.
evidence: "That's not in the file," Asha said carefully.

value.name: Daniel dismisses codicil claim
value.description: Daniel rejects the implication of a hidden codicil, arguing that Pinsky's retired practice would have forwarded any such document to the bank.
evidence: "This is ridiculous," Daniel said. "Pinsky retired in October. He had a stroke. His practice was absorbed by, what, Hennessey and someone. If there was a codicil, they would have it. They sent everything to the bank."

value.name: Asha challenges completeness of records
value.description: Asha begins to respond by implying that only the documents actually possessed were forwarded, suggesting the record may be incomplete.
